public_rationale: Press reports name SpaceX and Microsoft as the two customers behind about a fifth of Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue (e1). SpaceX owns Cursor and xAI and competes with Anthropic through Grok (e2). In October 2026 The Information reported that Meta and Microsoft are actively moving staff off Claude and onto their own tools. The same report covers Meta's Muse Spark models and its Muse Code rival to Claude Code (e3). The claim is an 'and/or' statement, so building rivals or cutting Claude use is enough, and both are reported. One caveat: the reports describe sharp cuts in internal use, not a full exit. Claude use through Microsoft's platforms is still growing (e4). 'Dropping' is a slightly strong word, but the core claim holds.
limitations: Customer identities and the Meta and Microsoft cuts come from press reports, mostly second-hand accounts of The Information, not company statements.
Whether Meta ranks among the very largest customers is not shown in a filing.
The claim that SpaceX could kick Anthropic off its infrastructure was not checked. It is context, not the claim being graded.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic's largest customers are building competing models or discussing dropping its services.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic’s largest customers are also explicitly building competitors and/or actively discussing dropping their services.

from_speaker: and/or actively discussing dropping their services
Meta and Microsoft have explicitly discussed dropping their Anthropic use
our_interpretation: This describes an ongoing state at the post date (2026-10-28). I use the period from June 2026 through the post date. That covers the latest customer-concentration data (first half of 2026) and the October 2026 reports on Meta and Microsoft. October news is not excluded.
'Largest customers' means companies that credible reporting names as among Anthropic's biggest revenue sources. Here those are SpaceX/Cursor, Microsoft and Meta.

The claim is a disjunction ('and/or'). It holds if the largest customers are building rival models or products, or are publicly reported to be cutting or moving away from Claude. Each customer does not need to do both.
'Discussing dropping' is read as credible reporting that a customer is steering staff off Claude or cutting Claude use and spending. A full contract cancellation is not required.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports that Anthropic's top customers (such as SpaceX/Cursor and Microsoft, and Meta) own or build rival AI models or tools, or are cutting or winding down their use of Claude.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that these companies are not among Anthropic's largest customers, or that none of them builds competing models or tools and none is reported to be cutting or dropping Claude.

evidence.excerpt: about a fifth of its revenue in the first half of 2026 came from just two customers. Anthropic didn't name either company in its S-1 filing, but several industry reports have identified them as SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT).
evidence.publisher: The Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance
evidence.explanation: Shows that SpaceX (through Cursor) and Microsoft are reported to be Anthropic's two largest customers. This sets up the 'largest customers' part of the claim.

evidence.excerpt: It now owns xAI and Cursor, putting it in direct competition with Anthropic in foundation models through Grok and in AI coding tools through Cursor
evidence.explanation: Shows that SpaceX, a top customer through Cursor, owns and builds the rival Grok models. This matches 'SpaceX (which owns Cursor) has Grok'.

evidence.excerpt: Tech giants Meta Platforms and Microsoft are actively reducing their internal reliance on Anthropic's Claude AI technology as both companies steer employees toward their own in-house artificial intelligence tools
evidence.publisher: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance (citing The Information)
evidence.explanation: Shows that Meta and Microsoft are actively moving staff off Claude and onto their own tools. That fits 'discussing dropping their services', though it is a cut rather than a full exit.

evidence.excerpt: this reduction applies exclusively to internal operations; customer spending on Anthropic models via Microsoft's enterprise platforms continues to see steady growth.
evidence.publisher: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance (citing The Information)
evidence.explanation: Limits the 'dropping' part. Microsoft is cutting its own staff use, but resale of Claude through Microsoft platforms is growing. So Microsoft is not dropping Anthropic as a whole.
